title: Dispatch: structured justification, enforced pack-authority rejection, multi-valued hooks (attempt 9)
description:
Fresh full review of PR #476 at b738078: three implementation blockers and one
contract blocker. The single-valued hook relation is a NEW DEFECT CLASS, so the
contract has been updated by the supervisor and the next review is a FRESH FULL
review. Another new class in that review forces rescope or design reopening —
this is the last round before that.

CLOSED BY THE PREVIOUS ROUND — do not touch: canonical roster validation
preventing closure after deleting obligations; all 68 rows underived; unknown
capability-hook names failing closed; forbidden-total detection traversing
arrays.

FINDING 1 (contract staleness) IS ALREADY FIXED by the supervisor — the bead
contract now states 0 derived / 68 underived. Nothing for you there.

=== FILES YOU OWN ===
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/finding-registry.json
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/finding-registry.md
  packages/core/src/rules/findingRegistry.ts
  packages/core/test/findingRegistry.test.ts

=== F2: PACK SELF-DERIVATION IS STILL ADMISSIBLE ===
The documentation says a pack query can never establish authoritative
membership, but the validator still lets ANY registered pack generator make a
row derived, and the all-derived test explicitly expects pack-generated rows to
STOP BLOCKING. Documented intent with no enforcement is not a rule.

FIX: the validator must REJECT pack self-derivation. A registered pack generator
may supply CURRENT membership for comparison against an independent authority;
it may never be the authority that makes a row derived. The test that expects
pack-generated rows to stop blocking encodes the defect — change it deliberately
and record why. Add a positive test: a row whose only authority is a pack
generator must remain underived and must block closure.

=== F3: THE ANTI-TEMPLATE GUARD IS EVADED AGAIN — CHANGE THE APPROACH ===
The normalizer EXCLUDES the newly introduced substitution fields (title,
authority, source scope) and merely blacklists the previous revision's exact
sentences. Consecutive checked-in rows still share identical sentence structures
with substituted values.

This is the FOURTH evasion: an identical sentence across 61 rows, then
round-robin audit aliases, then title-substituted reasons, now a normalizer with
holes plus a sentence blacklist. Every previous fix hardened the detector and
every one was evaded within a round.

*** SUPERVISOR DECISION — STOP HARDENING THE DETECTOR. ***
A prose field derived from a row's own metadata carries no independent
information, so it will always be templatable. Replace it:

  underivedReason becomes STRUCTURED —
    cause:      a CLOSED ENUM of blocking causes (e.g. requires-audit-prose-
                reconciliation, requires-clause-ir, requires-external-source,
                requires-engine-capability). Choose the real set from the 68
                rows; do not invent an 'other' escape hatch.
    blockedBy:  a RESOLVABLE reference — a bead ID or artifact path that must
                exist. Validate that it resolves.

A structured value either resolves or does not; it cannot be paraphrased into
looking distinct. Delete the sentence blacklist and the prose normalizer with
it — keeping them alongside the structured field just preserves the arms race.

Apply the same reasoning to `invariant` if it is also mechanically generated:
if its content is derivable from the row's own metadata, it is not carrying
information and should be structured or removed. Report your judgement either
way.

=== F4 (NEW DEFECT CLASS): HOOKS ARE RESTRICTED TO ONE PRIMITIVE ===
Several hooks semantically span multiple canonical primitives, and the relation
keeps only one, silently dropping the rest:
  engine:F10 currency/property/inventory/XP -> maps only to currency mutation,
             although the roster separately requires retained-asset creation;
  engine:F5  storage/charge/reset            -> same loss;
  engine:F9  quantity-cost/area-targeting    -> same loss.
FIX: make the hook-to-primitive relation MULTI-VALUED — a hook maps to every
canonical primitive it covers. A hook whose primitives cannot all be determined
must FAIL CLOSED rather than picking one. Audit every hook in the relation for
dropped primitives, not just the three named. Add tests asserting the full
primitive set for each multi-primitive hook, and a fail-closed test for an
indeterminate hook.

=== PRESERVE ===
68 rows and 70 aliases each resolving once; the durable obligation/target/
invariant vs violation split; canonical roster closure validation; qualified
engine capability targets; the fail-closed gate with blocker-identity
assertions; array-traversing forbidden-total detection.

=== ENVIRONMENT / CONSTRAINTS ===
npm ci first; npm run verify:worktree BEFORE committing. Edit only the four files
above. A sibling dispatch runs on PR #477. Do not touch package.json,
internal.ts, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .github/, or any script/CI file. Do not
regenerate the pack or run the importer. Do not modify any bead but your own; no
bd dolt push; no push, PR comment, or merge. The PR body and the bead contract
are the supervisor's to maintain.
acceptance_criteria:
• The validator rejects pack self-derivation; a row whose only authority is a pack generator stays underived and blocks closure, with a positive test.
• The test expecting pack-generated rows to stop blocking is deliberately changed, with the reason recorded.
• underivedReason is structured: a closed enum cause plus a resolvable blockedBy reference, validated to resolve; the prose normalizer and sentence blacklist are deleted.
• A judgement is recorded on whether invariant is likewise mechanically generated, and it is structured or removed if so.
• The hook-to-primitive relation is multi-valued; every hook is audited for dropped primitives; an indeterminate hook fails closed.
• Tests assert the full primitive set for each multi-primitive hook and fail-closed behaviour for an indeterminate one.
• All preserved behaviour and tests survive.
• npm run verify:worktree passes.
notes: Completion report: Implemented the binding re-architecture in the four owned files. Replaced prose underivedReason values with a closed cause enum plus a resolvable blockedBy reference; replaced mechanically generated invariant prose with a typed source-semantic-preservation contract linked to audit authority; removed the prose normalizer and sentence blacklist; rejected every pack-* generator as an authority for derived membership while retaining current-pack joins; changed the exact hook relation to multi-valued, audited compound F4/F5/F9/F10 hooks, emitted one qualified capability identity per primitive, and added fail-closed unknown/near-match/multi-primitive tests; preserved roster, aliases, identity snapshots, closure blockers, and recursive total checks. Decision disagreement: none; I followed the supervisor design. Obligations not satisfied: none within the owned acceptance criteria. The 68-row source/audit membership derivation and executable violation predicates remain intentionally out of scope under the binding decomposition and were not implemented here. Verification passed via npm run verify:worktree (263 files passed, 4 skipped; 4727 tests passed, 19 skipped). Commit: 5696aa1. Follow-up: eshyra-oeur for later shared capability-ledger integration.
close_reason: Implemented and verified the structured registry, pack-authority rejection, and multi-valued hook design; completion report appended.
